WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
A Storm Surge Warning is in effect for...
* Bonita Beach northward to the Suwannee River, including Tampa Bay

A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Bonita Beach northward to the mouth of the Suwannee River

Interests elsewhere in the Florida peninsula and the southeastern
United States should monitor the progress of Milton.


DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 400 AM CDT (0900 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Milton was located near
latitude 22.4 North, longitude 90.0 West. Milton is moving toward the
east near 9 mph (15 km/h). A faster east-northeastward motion is
expected later today, followed by a northeastward motion by Wednesday
night. On the forecast track, the center of Milton will move across
the southeastern Gulf of Mexico today and reach the west coast of
Florida by late Wednesday.

Maximum sustained winds are near 160 mph (260 km/h) with higher gusts.
Milton is an extremely dangerous category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-
Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Some weakening is expected before
landfall, but Milton is forecast to be a dangerous major hurricane
when it reaches the west coast of Florida.

Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center, and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles
(150 km).

The estimated minimum central pressure is 905 mb (26.73 inches).


HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
STORM SURGE: Life-threatening storm surge is expected along portions
of the west coast of the Florida Peninsula. The combination of a
dangerous storm surge and the tide will cause normally dry areas near
the coast to be flooded by rising waters moving inland from the
shoreline.

WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected within the Hurricane Warning
area in west-central Florida by late Wednesday, with tropical storm
conditions beginning Wednesday morning.

RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Milton is expected to produce total
rainfall accumulations of 5 to 10 inches with localized totals up to
15 inches across portions of Florida and the Florida Keys.
